title: You just found $20 million — Part 2
style: Warm painterly 2D cartoon illustration, cinematic graphic-novel look: clean bold dark outlines, rich textured digital painting, soft volumetric light, deep warm oranges and moody blues, detailed environment, vertical 9:16 composition.
character: MAIN CHARACTER: a lanky ADULT man drawn as a minimalist cartoon: a perfectly round smooth tan head, two tiny solid black dot eyes set wide apart, short thin eyebrow strokes, a very small simple mouth, no nose, no visible hair, simple long limbs, dark charcoal baseball cap, oversized heather-grey hoodie, black slim pants, white sneakers. Minimal face like a webcomic, not a child, not anime, no big eyes.

scenes.A: Night, an empty concrete parking garage, a single black car with its headlights on, the man walking toward it carrying a heavy black duffel bag, long shadows.
scenes.B: A tall man in a long grey coat and gloves standing by the black car unzipping the duffel bag and looking at the cash, cold fluorescent garage light, the main character watching nervously.
scenes.C: The man kneeling on his living room rug at night digging through an open duffel bag of cash, warm lamp light, worried.

D.prompt: First-person point of view from the viewer's own eyes: no face, no head and no full body visible, only the viewer's own two cartoon hands in grey hoodie sleeves reaching in from the bottom of the frame. The hands hold a small black GPS tracker with a blinking red light pulled from under stacks of cash in a duffel bag.

scenes.E: The man carrying a black duffel bag up the steps of a police station at night, blue and red lights reflecting, determined.
scenes.F: Police officers in a parking garage at dawn surrounding the black car, the man in the grey coat in handcuffs, flashing lights.
scenes.G: Close-up portrait of the man facing the viewer, relieved small smile, sunrise light through a window behind him.

segments.text: Eleven fifty-eight p.m. 18 Mercer Road is an empty parking garage. One car. Headlights on.
A man in a grey coat takes the bag. Counts it. Then he says: check your bag.
At home, you dig to the bottom of the bag you kept.
They were never letting you keep it. They needed someone to move the money for them.
So you drive both the bag and the tracker straight to the police.
The money was stolen. By morning, the tracker leads them back to that garage.
The bank's reward for its return? Two hundred and fifty thousand dollars. Legally yours.
Sometimes the best twist is the one nobody picks. The end.
